title.analysis: Authentic title "What Changes at $1M, $2M, and $5M Retirement?" is a tiered-threshold question frame. The script delivers a dense, mostly accurate tour of how Social Security share, taxes, RMDs, IRMAA, estate rules and fees change by portfolio size, plus behavioural evidence that wealthier retirees under-spend. TYPICAL at the 0.5 boundary (0.50009x) against a very young cohort; association only, no CTR evidence.

script.opening_words: You're at a restaurant on a Tuesday. Laminated dessert menus, a booth that sticks to the back of your arm, a couple to your left, a couple to your right, both ordering the $22 salmon. The couple on your left retired with $1.1 million. The couple on your right retired with 4.9. And the couple on your right is the one who picks up the check, turns it toward the window, and reads it twice. That's not a joke about
script.ending_words: the answer is nothing, find that out now while you still have the 20 years to spend on something else. And if it's something specific, something you can picture, then you know what you're climbing toward and the number is just logistics. Everything here is observation and arithmetic, not advice, and every figure has a date on it. Verify anything you plan to act on. So go find your Wednesday.
script.analysis: Full 19394 canonical characters read. A tiered retirement explainer using three composite retirees (Wendy $1M, Theo $2M, Naomi $5M): restaurant hook, system framing, reality check (Fidelity and Fed medians vs means), $1M (Social Security as an annuity, 0% gains, senior deduction, sequence risk, Bengen vs Morningstar), $2M (RMDs, Social Security taxation, IRMAA, long-term care), the under-spending finding (EBRI, J.P. Morgan, Blanchett), $5M (Social Security share, RMDs, NIIT, Roth conversion inversion, state estate taxes, fees), the cost of the jump in years, happiness research, inflation and a close. Verified: EBRI spend-down, Fidelity year-end 2025 averages. Reproduces: RMDs, Social Security shares, $5.4M threshold, fee and flat-fee ratios, 8/12-year jumps, nursing-home share, inflation. Minor issues: Fidelity figures one quarter stale; "1% eats 30%" (24.5% at 7%); several statistics unfetched. The stored ending is complete.
beat_map: Hook: two couples, $1.1M vs $4.9M, reading the check.
$1M: Social Security as an asset; 0% gains; senior deduction.
$5M: Social Security share, RMDs, NIIT, Roth conversions.
Cost of the jump in years; happiness; inflation.
Close: what would you do on Wednesday.
